_why: Gzipped transfer ceilings per game. The mission is that these games are reachable on metered data, so bytes need something that refuses them. Ceilings are measured-today plus ~8% headroom, deliberately not an aspiration: a budget nobody can meet gets raised until it means nothing.
_knownWins: DONE: audio was WAV (uncompressed PCM) at 855-1270 KB gzipped per game, larger than the Phaser engine. Re-encoded to Ogg/Opus with an AAC/m4a fallback: 4352 KB of WAV became 775 KB of Opus or 862 KB of AAC, and a browser downloads only one of the pair.

DONE (partial): champs no longer PRELOADS its two Korean weights. That dropped its cold load from 1226.8 KB to 158.6 KB - the first wait no longer carries 1.09 MB of typography. The faces still load via font-display: swap and are precached by the service worker, which installs in the background after load, so offline text does not fall back to a system face.
_audioNote: The audio figure counts BOTH shipped formats, so it OVERSTATES what a player pays by roughly half. That is deliberate: a ceiling that over-counts fails safe, where one that guessed which format a player gets could pass a real regression.

_blocked.item: Subsetting the Korean webfonts to the glyphs actually used.
_blocked.size: Measured per glyph, which cancels out how much Korean a game happens to show: champs 484 distinct Korean characters in 1068.7 KB (2261 B/glyph), lastwar 393 in 544.7 KB (1419), kingshot 331 in 492.9 KB (1525), against whiteout 421 in 74.6 KB (182). So champs carries 12.5x, kingshot 8.4x and lastwar 7.8x what whiteout pays for the same job.
_blocked.not_a_vocabulary_difference: whiteout needs 421 distinct Korean characters and champs 484 - essentially the same set. The gap is unsubset weight, not a larger vocabulary, so the saving does not cost any displayable text. Two of the three files are even NAMED .subset.woff2 while carrying a near-full syllable block.
_blocked.glyph_sets_are_derived: scripts/font-glyphs.mjs reads every shipped source file and writes the exact character set each game can display to site/font-glyphs/<slug>.txt - which is what pyftsubset takes as --text-file. Verified against every text file in every package: zero characters that a game renders are missing from its own list, so subsetting to these lists cannot turn in-game text into tofu. Test files are excluded because they are never downloaded, and design docs because they are not either.
_blocked.why_blocked: No subsetter is available on this host and installing one is not the agent's to do. Checked and absent: pyftsubset, hb-subset, fonttools, woff2_compress and sfnt2woff on PATH; fontTools in system python; any font-parsing package in node_modules. python brotli IS present, but that is woff2 compression only and cannot rebuild a glyph table.
_blocked.needs_from_the_user: Approval to install a font toolchain - python3 fonttools with brotli (giving pyftsubset), or the harfbuzz hb-subset binary. `node scripts/font-glyphs.mjs` then prints the exact command per font.
_blocked.deliberately_not_done: Hand-rolling a woff2 parser. Font binary formats are exactly where an approximate implementation ships a subtly broken glyph table, and it would break Korean text for precisely the metered-data players the subsetting is for. The saving does not justify that risk.
_blocked.separate_finding: 25 Korean characters appear only in game.json titleKo/summaryKo. Those are drawn by the LANDING PAGE, which loads no Korean webfont at all, so the catalogue titles fall back to whatever Korean face the device has. On a low-end Android without one that is tofu on the storefront. Adding a face there is a transfer-size decision for the user, not a subsetting task.
